sections.heading: 1. Safety and Access
sections.content: All personnel must wear an ID badge. Visitors require escort approval from the shift supervisor.

sections.heading: 1.1 Access Levels
sections.content: Level A allows office access only. Level B allows server hall access. Level C allows server hall and power room access.

sections.heading: 1.2 Emergency Evacuation
sections.content: On fire alarm, evacuate through marked routes and assemble at Point North. The shift lead performs headcount within 7 minutes.

sections.heading: 2. Maintenance Overview
sections.content: Scheduled maintenance occurs every second Tuesday between 01:00 and 03:00 UTC.

sections.heading: 2.1 Pre-Maintenance Checklist
sections.content: Confirm backup completion, notify stakeholders 24 hours in advance, and verify rollback snapshots.

sections.heading: 2.2 Post-Maintenance Verification
sections.content: Run health checks for CPU, memory, and storage latency. Close the change ticket only after all checks pass.

sections.heading: 3. Incident Classification
sections.content: Severity 1 affects critical customer services, Severity 2 affects non-critical services, and Severity 3 is minor degradation.

sections.heading: 3.1 Initial Response
sections.content: Acknowledge alerts within 5 minutes. Open an incident bridge for Severity 1 and Severity 2 events.

sections.heading: 3.2 Communication Cadence
sections.content: For Severity 1 incidents, publish status updates every 15 minutes. For Severity 2, every 30 minutes.

sections.heading: 4. Backup Policy
sections.content: Incremental backups run daily at 02:00 UTC. Full backups run every Sunday at 03:00 UTC.

sections.heading: 4.1 Retention
sections.content: Keep daily incremental backups for 14 days and weekly full backups for 12 weeks.

sections.heading: 4.2 Recovery Test
sections.content: Perform a recovery drill on the first business day of each quarter and document recovery time objective results.

sections.heading: 5. Change Categories
sections.content: Standard changes are pre-approved, normal changes require review board approval, and emergency changes are approved by the duty manager.

sections.heading: 5.1 Lead Times
sections.content: Submit normal changes at least 3 business days before implementation. Emergency changes may be implemented immediately with retrospective review.

sections.heading: 5.2 Documentation
sections.content: Every change request must include risk assessment, rollback plan, owner, and validation steps.

sections.heading: 6. Alert Priorities
sections.content: P1 alerts indicate service outage, P2 alerts indicate major performance degradation, and P3 alerts indicate warning conditions.

sections.heading: 6.1 On-Call Rotation
sections.content: Primary on-call rotates weekly every Monday at 09:00 UTC. Secondary on-call must acknowledge escalation within 10 minutes.

sections.heading: 6.2 Alert Tuning
sections.content: Review noisy alerts monthly and require at least 7 days of post-change monitoring after threshold adjustments.
